1_SCENE_OVERVIEW.where: A brownstone street at dusk (SET-CITY-DUSK, provisional geography), ending on the lit windows of Halcyon House across the rooftops.
1_SCENE_OVERVIEW.what: Five inhabitants get ready for the night; a neighbour tries to film a woman dancing, his lens glows copper, he lowers it, and she raises a glass to him.
1_SCENE_OVERVIEW.why: Series opener: it shows the world and the Ember before any principal appears, and points the season at Halcyon House.
1_SCENE_OVERVIEW.emotionalObjective: Warmth and anticipation, with one small turn from intrusion to grace.

FADE IN:

EXT. CITY STREET — STREET — DUSK

High on a glass tower the low sun burns copper. Down below, a street of brownstones. Windows come on one by one, like a city putting on its earrings.

[[TIME: 4]]
[[MUSIC: A big band warming up somewhere out of sight: loose trumpet, a walking bass, brushes. Music only; no dialogue and no narration in this release.]]
[[SFX: Street bed: a bus sighing, a door, distant laughter.]]

EXT. CITY STREET — TAILOR'S SHOPFRONT — DUSK

[[ENTER: TAILOR]]

A tailor in shirtsleeves hauls down the grille on his shop. Halfway, he stops.

[[TIME: 2]]

Through the window, his hands straighten the lapel on the mannequin.

[[TIME: 2.25]]

The grille comes down. He pats the glass goodnight.

[[TIME: 1.5]]
[[EXIT: TAILOR]]

EXT. CITY STREET — BUS STOP — DUSK

[[ENTER: TEENAGER]]

A teenager at the bus stop tries a dance step in the shelter glass. Wrong.

[[TIME: 1.625]]

Wrong again.

[[TIME: 1.125]]

Right. He lands it on the beat and grins at his reflection. Nobody saw. Good.

[[TIME: 2.875]]
[[EXIT: TEENAGER]]

EXT. CITY STREET — FIRE ESCAPE — DUSK

[[ENTER: GRANDMOTHER]]

A jewel-green dress unfurls over a fire-escape rail.

[[TIME: 2.5]]

A grandmother smooths the skirt with both hands.

[[TIME: 1.5]]

She gives it a long look, as if the dress has a date tonight and she approves of him.

[[TIME: 2.625]]
[[EXIT: GRANDMOTHER]]

EXT. CITY STREET — BALCONY KITCHEN — DUSK

[[ENTER: WOMAN ON THE BALCONY]]

Through an open balcony door, a woman dances alone in her kitchen, a wooden spoon for a partner. A glass of wine waits on the ledge.

[[TIME: 2.75]]

She spins the spoon. Completely unembarrassed.

[[TIME: 1.75]]

EXT. CITY STREET — NEIGHBOUR'S WINDOW — DUSK

[[ENTER: NEIGHBOUR]]

Across the street, her neighbour lifts his phone toward her balcony.

[[TIME: 2]]
[[PROP: PR-NEIGHBOUR-PHONE: raised toward the balcony]]
[[MUSIC: The band thins to bass and brushes.]]

His lens blooms copper. The music stops dead.

[[TIME: 1.75]]
[[VFX: The lens blooms copper: the Ember, the city's everyday no.]]
[[SFX: No designed sound for the Ember. Only the street.]]

He lowers the phone, embarrassed.

[[TIME: 2]]
[[PROP: PR-NEIGHBOUR-PHONE: lowered]]

On her balcony, the woman has seen all of it. She lifts her glass to him across the street and goes back to her dance. The band comes back in.

[[TIME: 3]]
[[MUSIC: The groove returns as the glass goes up.]]

EXT. CITY STREET — ROOFTOPS — DUSK

[[SHOT: WIDE — RISING MOVE]]

The camera rises past her lit kitchen and the green dress on its rail, over water towers and fire escapes.

[[TIME: 3.5]]

Across the rooftops, the tall windows of a ballroom glow amber: Halcyon House.

[[TIME: 4.75]]
[[MUSIC: The band lands its first full chord as the windows come into view, and lets it ring.]]

CUT TO BLACK.

treatment.feel: A neighbourhood overture: five strangers getting ready for the same night, watched with affection.
treatment.perspective: Secret witness, then one point-of-view shot for the toast.
treatment.language: Locked-off vignettes, one gesture each; motion reserved for the opening tilt and the closing rise.
treatment.atmosphere: Dusk turning blue; copper light on glass gives way to amber windows.
treatment.rhythm: Four- to seven-second vignettes cut on action and beats; a slowed Ember beat in silence; one long rise into a ringing chord.

intent.dramaticPurpose: Open the season on the world before any principal: a city that gets ready for the night, and one everyday courtesy, the Ember, that lets people be seen without being captured.
intent.emotionalCenter: The woman on the balcony raising her glass to the neighbour who just tried to film her: grace answering a small intrusion, without a closed curtain.

characterObjectives.TAILOR: Leave the work looking right before he locks up.
characterObjectives.TEENAGER: Land the step for himself, with nobody watching.
characterObjectives.GRANDMOTHER: Have the dress ready for tonight, and approve of it.
characterObjectives.WOMAN ON THE BALCONY: Dance for herself, and stay unembarrassed when she is noticed.
characterObjectives.NEIGHBOUR: Capture something lovely on reflex, then stand down when the city says no.

intent.subtext: Being seen is not being captured. Everyone here is preparing to be looked at tonight, and the Ember protects the difference between an audience and a recording.
intent.powerDynamics: The phone holds power for one second; the copper glow takes it back without a word, and the woman decides how the moment ends by raising a glass.

informationControl.before: The audience knows nothing: no names, no house, no rules of this world.
informationControl.during: The audience learns one rule by watching it work: a copper glow on a lens means capture declined, and people respect it.
informationControl.after: The audience knows the city dresses for the night and that everyone is heading somewhere with lit ballroom windows.

intent.cinematicPointOfView: An affectionate secret witness: the camera sees each private moment from a respectful distance, then takes the neighbour's point of view once, at the moment he gives up the recording.

visualDramaturgy.blocking: Each inhabitant performs one private action alone; nobody shares a frame until the toast crosses the street.
visualDramaturgy.camera: Mostly locked off for the vignettes so the gestures carry; the camera only moves to open (tilt down) and to close (rise and push).
visualDramaturgy.light: Dusk compressed from golden to blue across the release; copper is the sun at the start and only the Ember at blue hour.
visualDramaturgy.costume: Everyday clothes on everyone except the jewel-green dress, which is the one garment dressed for the night.
visualDramaturgy.architecture: Brownstones, fire escapes and a balcony across from a window; geography held so the toast reads across a real street.
visualDramaturgy.editing: Vignettes of varied length, cuts on action and on beats, a held silence on the Ember, then one continuous rise to black.

intent.atmosphere: Warm, funny and unhurried: the last minute of daylight in a neighbourhood where people still dress up and still look out for each other.
intent.sonicIdentity: A big band warming up out of sight becomes the groove of the street, stops dead on the Ember, and returns as the real band heard from the ballroom.
intent.endingImpression: The audience should want to go where everyone is going: across the rooftops to the lit windows of Halcyon House, on a night that is about to begin.

spatial.name: Brownstone street at dusk
spatial.scale: Two-lane residential street about 18 m between facades; brownstones of four and five storeys; a glass tower stands at the west end.
spatial.orientation: The street runs east to west. North side, west to east: the tailor's shop at street level, the woman's converted brownstone with a fourth-floor balcony kitchen, the grandmother's brownstone with a third-floor fire escape. South side: the bus shelter and, directly across from the balcony, the neighbour's second-floor window. Halcyon House lies east beyond the rooftops.

9_FOUNDER_DECISIONS.question: Approve the S1-01 screenplay v2 (still DRAFT)?
9_FOUNDER_DECISIONS.why: Every shot, cue and keyframe is planned from v2; v1 is kept in SCREENPLAYS/HISTORY.
9_FOUNDER_DECISIONS.recommendation: Approve v2: the glass is set up, the Ember is silent and Halcyon House is windows only.

9_FOUNDER_DECISIONS.question: Music direction and composer route?
9_FOUNDER_DECISIONS.why: The cue arc and hit points are planned; who composes it decides cost, rights and how exactly it hits frame 324, 684 and 990.
options: fal ElevenLabs music (low cost; commercial terms to review)
9_FOUNDER_DECISIONS.recommendation: Commission a composer for the main theme; frame-exact hits are hard to prompt.

9_FOUNDER_DECISIONS.question: What does the Ember look like on a lens?
9_FOUNDER_DECISIONS.why: It holds for the season and must never be mistaken for the gold yes revealed in S1-58.
options: Soft copper bloom spreading from the lens
A thin copper ring around the lens
9_FOUNDER_DECISIONS.recommendation: Approve two KF-EMBER-LOOK candidates (80 credits) and choose one.

9_FOUNDER_DECISIONS.question: Halcyon House: windows only, or supply an exterior authority?
9_FOUNDER_DECISIONS.why: No approved exterior exists and the sprint forbids inventing one.
options: Windows only (no facade, roofline or signage)
Founder supplies an exterior reference first
9_FOUNDER_DECISIONS.recommendation: Windows only for S1-01; design the exterior when S1-02 to S1-05 need the front steps.

9_FOUNDER_DECISIONS.question: Design of the jewel-green dress?
9_FOUNDER_DECISIONS.why: It appears in four shots and the rise; it needs one fixed design (U-4).
9_FOUNDER_DECISIONS.recommendation: Two candidates (80 credits): a 1960s satin cocktail dress and a bias-cut evening dress.
9_FOUNDER_DECISIONS.note: Story continuity approved (founder, 2026-10-25); the design is chosen at S1-01 visual development, and the chosen garment is the one S1-77 uses (R-02). No candidate is chosen.

9_FOUNDER_DECISIONS.question: Approve the inhabitants' looks as planned (scene-scoped)?
9_FOUNDER_DECISIONS.why: Ages, looks and clothes are directorial interpretation; none of the five gets a permanent package.
9_FOUNDER_DECISIONS.recommendation: Approve; faces are fixed by each vignette's first start frame.
9_FOUNDER_DECISIONS.answer: RECURRING (founder, 2026-10-25): the tailor, the grandmother and the teenager keep reusable recurring-background identities; the woman on the balcony and the neighbour stay scene-scoped.

9_FOUNDER_DECISIONS.question: Is the tailor Wendell Ames?
9_FOUNDER_DECISIONS.why: Yes makes him a recurring character whose identity reference must exist before S1-01 frames are generated.
9_FOUNDER_DECISIONS.answer: No: an unnamed tailor (ANONYMOUS, founder, 2026-10-25). The shop sign stays unreadable.

9_FOUNDER_DECISIONS.question: How is the street seeded?
9_FOUNDER_DECISIONS.why: SET-CITY-DUSK has no approved reference; every frame derives from KF-ENV-CITY-DUSK-A.
options: Look development: two candidates from the spec
Founder supplies a street photograph as the reference
9_FOUNDER_DECISIONS.recommendation: Founder photograph if one exists; otherwise two look-development candidates (80 credits).

9_FOUNDER_DECISIONS.question: Confirm 24 fps delivery?
9_FOUNDER_DECISIONS.why: All timing is in frames at 24 fps, matching the recorded Kling outputs (PK-007).

9_FOUNDER_DECISIONS.question: Title card at the end?
9_FOUNDER_DECISIONS.why: The release ends on a ringing chord over black.

9_FOUNDER_DECISIONS.question: Authorize the generation budget?
9_FOUNDER_DECISIONS.why: No credits are spent until the founder authorizes an amount.
options: Authorize the estimate plus expected revisions
9_FOUNDER_DECISIONS.recommendation: Authorize references and keyframes first, then video once frames are approved.

9_FOUNDER_DECISIONS.question: Lock the teenager's four-count step?
9_FOUNDER_DECISIONS.why: SH05 to SH07 miss it, tangle it and land it on frame 324, and S1-51 repeats the same four counts (S-02, R-04). The step is not choreographed yet (CHOREOGRAPHY_LOCK_PENDING).
options: Founder supplies or approves the four counts
9_FOUNDER_DECISIONS.recommendation: Lock the step before the SH05 start frame is generated; no shot length changes.
